implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the CPA-owner is the only preparer and signer, so duties cannot be separated inside the practice. The client acts as the second approver: each client signs Form 8879 before the return is e-filed, and the POL-01 8.5 call-back rule confirms any refund bank, address, or email change on the number already on file. In filing season the owner compares returns filed under the firm's EFIN and PTIN with the firm's own count each Monday (POL-01 7.7). POL-01 4.5 adds an outside reviewer at least every second year.
evidence: POL-01 4.5, 7.7, and 8.5; signed Forms 8879 in SYS-02

implementation_statement: The laptop locks after 5 minutes idle and the phone after 1 minute; both need the password or passcode to unlock.

The IT consultant connects only when the owner starts and watches a remote-support session; there is no unattended access. A services agreement with security terms and the IRC 7216 written notice exist since 2026-07-23. Gap: whether the consultant's remote-support account uses MFA is not yet confirmed.

The owner has only CPE ethics training. By 2026-11-30 the owner completes a security course with phishing and business email compromise modules, reads IRS Security Summit and Pub. 4557 reminders, and repeats the course each year before filing season.

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the change control element is the change log in the security log (POL-01 7.8). Each change to a security setting (MFA, sharing, forwarding, device encryption, router) is written down with the date and reason and must not weaken a POL-01 rule unless an exception is approved under POL-01 5.4. Gap: the 2024 change that turned off mailbox MFA was made without review. Target 2026-10-31 (P03 G-020).
evidence: POL-01 5.4 and 7.8; security log (planned); P03 G-020

implementation_statement: POL-01 Appendix A lists every device, SaaS service, and place where client information is kept (adopted 2026-08-31). Gap: the phone's personal photo backup and old laptop download folders still hold client documents until the cleanup due 2027-01-15.

The BIA (P05), the POL-01 contingency section, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gap: no practice continuation agreement with another CPA and no stored recovery codes (due 2026-12-31 and 2026-09-30).

The tax software vendor backs up returns and portal documents (inherited; RPO 1 hour in its SOC 2 system description). Owner responsibility: the email and file suite has only 30 days of version history and laptop files have no backup. An encrypted backup service for the suite with one-year retention is due 2026-11-30.
Every service has a named account for the owner; the owner never shares credentials. Clients use their own portal accounts.

implementation_statement: Paper is cross-cut shredded in the home office. Gap: no procedure or record for wiping old laptops, phones, or the printer-scanner, and paper back to 2019 is kept with no schedule.
The home office is a separate room locked when the owner is away; paper client files are kept in a locked cabinet. Clients meet the owner in the office by appointment only.

POL-01 sections 8 and 9 set the rules for client information, devices, and AI tools (adopted 2026-08-31). Gap: family devices share the home network and the AI assistant was used with client documents before the rules existed.
First risk assessment completed 2026-07-31 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01). A written assessment is not mandatory under 314.6, but the owner keeps one. Reviewed each July and after major changes.

Contracts with data protection terms exist for the tax software, the email suite, and (since 2026-07-23) the IT consultant. The tax software vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed 2026-07-28. Gap: no vendor list; the practice management and AI assistant terms were never reviewed; no periodic assessment.

The laptop's built-in host firewall is on. Gap: the home office shares one network with family and smart-home devices, and the router admin password is the default. A separate network for the office devices and a new admin password are due 2026-10-31.

implementation_statement: The tax software, portal, and SaaS sessions use TLS (inherited). Gap: clients send documents as plain email attachments and text-message photos, and returns are emailed as attachments on request. Portal-only exchange for returns and source documents by 2027-01-15.

The laptop uses full-disk encryption and the phone is encrypted by its passcode; the SaaS providers encrypt stored data (tax software confirmed in its SOC 2 report). Client documents in the phone's personal photo backup are a data location problem tracked under CM-8.
evidence: Device encryption status; vendor SOC 2 report

implementation_statement: The SaaS vendors patch their services. Automatic updates are on for the laptop and phone; the owner restarts when prompted. Router firmware is covered under SC-7.
The laptop's built-in antivirus runs real-time and scheduled scans with automatic updates and quarantines detections. Owner responsibility: keep it on and act on alerts.

No retention schedule exists; files go back to 2014. POL-01 8.9 sets the rule; the written schedule is due 2026-12-31 (keeping Forms 8879 at least 3 years under Pub. 1345) and the first purge 2027-06-30.
